verdict.rationale: Stagehand documents CDP interop through `localBrowser.connect`, which attaches to any Chromium browser you are already running by URL. Existing Playwright/CDP-driven browsers can therefore be shared with Stagehand rather than rewritten, and the docs say you can use familiar page methods. However, the evidence shows Stagehand attaching to your browser, not your existing Playwright/Puppeteer code connecting to Stagehand- or Browserbase-hosted browsers. Missing for 10: a documented CDP/WebSocket endpoint for connecting external Playwright/Puppeteer clients to the product's browsers, explicit Playwright/Puppeteer compatibility docs, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can connect my existing Playwright, Puppeteer, or CDP automation code to the product's browsers instead of rewriting it

citations.quote: Attach over CDP (localBrowser.connect): Attach to any Chromium browser you are already running, by URL
When you know the selector or want zero inference, use page methods you already know.
